messages:
Nora (prod): Quick announce: published 'On-Prem Session Audit Mode' guidance to the KB. This gives customers an option to enable short-lived session traces for support without storing full prompts long-term. Link: https://internal.kb/redwood/onprem-session-audit

Sam B.: Does this change the default retention? We have customers asking for 7-day vs 90-day windows.

Nora (prod): Default stays 90d for full-audit. Session Audit Mode defaults to 7d and is opt-in. Important: session traces are hashed and references are reversible only with customer consent (see crypto appendix).

infra-bot: New KB entry posted: /kb/onprem-session-audit-2026-03-23  reviewers requested: eng-infra, security, support

Lina (security): Reviewed. Need stronger language around key escrow and who can request reconstitution of traces. Added comments to section 3.2. Also, add an explicit 'no external backups' clause for scoped sessions.

Hector (support): For ops: we added a support workflow that requires customer-signed consent before we rehydrate a session trace. There's a sample consent email in the KB and a CLI snippet to request a trace.

```
# request trace (support cli)
redwood support request-trace --cluster mycluster --session-id 1234abcd --consent-file consent.pdf
```

Sam B.: Will this impact metrics dashboards? Our dashboards rely on sample prompts for model drift alerts.

Nora (prod): We keep aggregated token metrics for drift detection; the session audit flag only affects raw-text retention. Dashboards are unaffected.

Lina (security): Action items: (1) @Nora update consent wording per my comments by Wed EOD, (2) @Hector add the CLI sample to the support runbook, (3) eng-infra to validate no backup processes capture traces. React with :white_check_mark: when done.
